Cases of COVID-19 and deaths related to COVID-19 continue to proliferate globally,
nationally, and locally. The WHO reports more than 4.2 million worldwide infections and more
than 292,000 related deaths. According to the United States Centers for Disease Control and
Prevention (“CDC”), more than 1.3 million people have been infected in the United States,
including confirmed cases in every state, with more than 83,000 related deaths. The numbers of
reported cases and deaths are continuing to increase dangerously throughout the United States and
in many parts of the world. It is also highly likely that there are many unreported cases and deaths.
Despite some hopeful signs in recent weeks, the numbers have also risen steadily in our
State since I declared a public health emergency. As of May 14, 2020, the New Mexico
Department of Health reported 5,503 confirmed cases of COVID-19 in New Mexico and at least
242 related deaths. Unfortunately, the number of deaths in our State has more than doubled since
the last extension of the public health emergency approximately two weeks ago. There are
confirmed cases of COVID-19 in 30 of New Mexico’s 33 counties. Despite proactive measures
taken by the State and our citizens, the increases in cases and deaths present a significant risk and
COVID-19 is expected to continue its spread in New Mexico.
Public health organizations have implemented emergency measures intended to slow the
spread of COVID-19. For example, on January 20, 2020, the CDC activated its Emergency
Operations Center in response to the COVID-19 outbreak. The WHO declared a Public Health
Emergency of International Concern shortly thereafter. Nearly all or our sister states have declared
a state of emergency and implemented significant measures and deployed substantial resources to
fight the spread of COVID-19.
New Mexico has taken aggressive measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19 and to
mitigate its potentially devastating effects. I have been in frequent contact with federal and state

agencies and officials who are coordinating their efforts and resources to fight COVID-19.
Various state agencies have been at the forefront of our State’s response to COVID-19, particularly
the New Mexico Department of Health.
Due to the continued spread of the COVID-19, it is necessary for all branches of State
government to continue taking actions to minimize the spread of COVID-19 and to reduce its
attendant physical and economic harms.
Therefore, for the reasons above, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New
Mexico, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of
New Mexico, hereby ORDER and DIRECT:
1. In consultation with the New Mexico Department of Health, I have determined that
the statewide public health emergency proclaimed in Executive Order 2020-004, and renewed in
Executive Orders 2020-022 and 2020-026, shall be renewed and extended through May 31, 2020.
2. All other powers invoked, directives, and orders contained in Executive Order
2020-004 remain in effect.
3. All other Executive Orders with a duration that was tied to the COVID-19 public
health emergency or that was not explicitly stated shall continue with the same effect, including
any orders appropriating emergency funding and the following orders: Executive Order 2020-012;
Executive Order 2020-013; Executive Order 2020-016; Executive Order 2020-017; Executive
Order 2020-020; Executive Order 2020-021; Executive Order 2020-024; and Executive Order
2020-025.
This Order supersedes any previous orders, proclamations, or directives in conflict. This
Executive Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until June 1, 2020 unless
renewed or until the Governor rescinds it.

State of Public Health Emergency and Invoking the Powers Provided by the All Hazard
Emergency Management Act and the Emergency Licensing Act, Executive Order 2020-004. That
Order is incorporated by reference herein.
WHEREAS, despite the best efforts of our State and local governments and the citizens
of New Mexico, COVID-19 has continued to spread and ongoing efforts are still necessary to
mitigate and contain the spread of COVID-19;
WHEREAS, many of the current confirmed positive cases of COVID-19 in New Mexico
have resulted from interstate and international travel to New Mexico. Because some individuals
infected with COVID-19 are asymptomatic or have very mild symptoms, travelers may be unaware
they are carrying the virus. For this reason, persons arriving in New Mexico from out of state must
self-isolate for a period of time sufficient to ensure that the public health and safety is not
jeopardized.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-019
ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF IN MEMORIAL
OF THE HONORABLE J. PAUL TAYLOR
On February 12, 2023, the Honorable J. Paul Taylor passed away at the age of 102.
Representative Taylor served the State and his community in the New Mexico House of
Representatives for eighteen years as the “conscience of the Legislature.” A longtime educator,
Representative Taylor was known for championing New Mexico’s people and culture.
Representative Taylor is a true state treasure, and his legacy of service will endure. It is appropriate
and proper to acknowledge Representative Taylor’s remarkable life and service through a public
period of mourning across New Mexico.
THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff beginning February 13, 2023, and
lasting though sundown of February 15, 2023. This action will serve to commemorate
Representative Taylor’s distinguished life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-082
ESTABLISHING THE VETERANS ADVISORY COUNCIL
WHEREAS, the State of New Mexico is committed to honoring and supporting its
veterans who have bravely served our nation;
WHEREAS, veterans face unique challenges reintegrating into civilian life, such as
finding meaningful employment, accessing quality healthcare, and navigating obtaining the
services and benefits to which they are entitled;
WHEREAS, it is imperative to address the needs and challenges faced by veterans and
ensure they receive the necessary support and services they deserve; and
WHEREAS, an advisory council comprising of veterans and individuals with expertise in
veterans affairs will provide valuable insights that can be used to eliminate gaps in services,
address areas for improvement, and develop innovative strategies to enhance the wellness of our
veterans.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the Laws of the State of New Mexico do
hereby ORDER and DIRECT as follows:
1. Creation; Membership. The Veterans Advisory Council (the “Council”) is hereby
established and administratively attached to the Department of Veterans Services. The Council

shall consist of eleven members with experience receiving or providing veterans services.
Members shall be appointed by the Governor for staggered terms of three years.
2. Council Duties. The Council shall:
A. Conduct research, gather information, and analyze data related to veterans'
needs, including but not limited to healthcare, mental health, education, employment,
housing, and legal services;
B. Review existing policies, programs, and services provided by state
agencies, non-profit organizations, and private entities to identify areas for improvement
and recommend strategies to address gaps in support for veterans;
C. Consult with veterans, their families, and relevant stakeholders to gather
input and understand the diverse needs and perspectives of the veteran community; and
D. Perform any other actions, as directed by the Secretary of the Department
of Veterans Services.
3. Annual Report. By June 1, 2024, and each June 1 thereafter, the Council shall
prepare and submit a report to the Governor and the Secretary of the Department of Veterans
Services summarizing the Council’s findings, recommendations, and any pro

A. The members shall not be compensated for their service, other than per diem
allowed under the Per Diem and Mileage Act.
B. The Secretary of the Department of Veterans Services shall designate the

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2024-192
AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION DUE TO WILDFIRES
AND FLOODING IN SAN MIGUEL AND MORA COUNTIES

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NMDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE an emergency situation exists in San Miguel and Mora Counties due to wildfires and
flooding and ORDER and DIRECT:

l. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, and welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extent they are in conflict.

3. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until all

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

AND FLOODING IN SAN MIGUEL AND MORA COUNTIES

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NMDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and

to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

OF TRANSPORTATION DUE TO WILDFIRES AND FLOODING IN
LINCOLN COUNTY

WHEREAS, Lincoln County was severely impacted by the South Fork Fire and Salt Fire,
both of which began on June 17, 2024;

WHEREAS, the South Fork Fire and Salt Fire burned over 25,000 acres, collectively;

WHEREAS, the Ruidoso Downs Racetrack is downstream of a watershed in Lincoln
County that was severely impacted by the South Fork Fire and Salt Fire;

WHEREAS, monsoonal rain patterns have repeatedly impacted the South Fork Fire and
Salt Fire burn scars—which interact with four other active burn scars in the region—producing
high levels of mudflow and debris flow that are continuously threatening public infrastructure and
residences;

WHEREAS, the postfire debris flows into a water channel that goes directly through the
Ruidoso Downs Racetrack, which has resulted in both a partial culvert collapse on the west end of
the racetrack, as well as a full collapse of a culvert at the east end of the racetrack;

WHEREAS, the culvert and road structure at the racetrack is in a state of complete failure
due to these collapses;

WHEREAS, segments of the structure are already flowing downstream, and the remaining

portions of the structure will very likely also flow downstream;

WHEREAS, these impacts pose a severe threat to the communities and public
infrastructure which lie directly upstream and downstream of the Racetrack; and

WHEREAS, this disaster is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control and requires
the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and to take
actions necessary to protect the public health, safety, and welfare.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico
do hereby DECLARE a state of emergency to exist in Lincoln County due to wildfires and
flooding, and ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the New Mexico Department of Transportation in accordance with NMSA 1978,
Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be
expended for the purposes of avoiding or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the
public health, safety, and welfare; and providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not
limited to, the payment of any expenses incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other
assistance to civil authorities. Such funds shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary
of Finance and Administration upon vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized
Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extent they are in conflict.

3. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until all

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2025-066

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role
in addressing this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora
County and San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for the NUDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol + Room 400 +* Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 * 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE an emergency situation exists and ORDER and DIRECT:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, and welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extent they are in conflict.

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

urgent need for the NMDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars

ORDER LOWERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF OFFICER TIMOTHY ONTIVEROS

Officer Timothy Ontiveros of the Bloomfield Police Department tragically lost his life after
being shot and killed in the line of duty while conducting a traffic stop on May 26, 2025. Officer
Ontiveros exemplified extraordinary bravery and unwavering dedication in serving and protecting
his fellow New Mexicans. He will be greatly missed by his family and community and will be
remembered as a dedicated father to his two daughters, a fighter and a true public servant. It is
appropriate and proper to acknowledge Officer Ontiveros’ life and service through a public period
of mourning across New Mexico.

NOW THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
do hereby ORDER and DIRECT that all United States and State flags be flown at half-staff
beginning June 5, 2025, and lasting through sundown of June 10, 2025. This action will serve to

commemorate Officer Ontiveros’ life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2025-292

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF DEPUTY ANTONIO ALEMAN

Deputy Antonio Aleman of the Dona Ana County Sheriffs Office tragically lost his life in
a car crash while on duty on July 8, 2025. Deputy Aleman served with courage, integrity, and a
steadfast commitment to the safety of all New Mexicans. He will be greatly missed by his family
and community and will be remembered as a dedicated husband and father to his two children. It
is appropriate and proper to acknowledge Deputy Aleman’s life and service through a public
period of mourning across New Mexico.

NOW THEREFORE, |, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New Mexico
and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all United States and State flags be flown at half-staff beginning July
15, 2025, and lasting through sundown of July 20, 2025. This action will serve to commemorate
Deputy Aleman’s life and to mourn his loss.

AND NATURAL RESOURCES DEPARTMENT

WHEREAS, wildland fires have or are occurring statewide, and conditions for wildland
fires are dangerous and expected to increase;

WHEREAS, these wildland fires are of such magnitude as to be beyond local control and

crews, as well as emergency action to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives
and property of the people of the State of New Mexico;

WHEREAS, the Forestry Division of the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources
Department is responsible for prevention and suppression of wildland fires on all non-federal and
non-municipal lands in the state, as authorized under the Forest Conservation Act, NMSA 1978,
Sections 68-2-1 to -25;

WHEREAS, the Forestry Division is designated as the agent of the State and authorized
to enter into contracts and agreements with the Secretary of the United States Department of

Agriculture and other state, federal, and private agencies or organizations to prevent and suppress

wildfires pursuant to NMSA 1978, Section 68-2-6;

WHEREAS, emergency funds are expended by the Forestry Division for the purposes of
pre-positioning resources, continuing the Governor’s Public Service Announcement to publicize
fire danger conditions and responding to wildland fires, and ensuring that preparation will be
adequate to deal with such disasters;

WHEREAS, the Forestry Division has incurred significant expenditures for personnel,
firefighters, supplies, and contract services for aircraft and equipment; and

WHEREAS, the Forestry Division requires additional funding at this time to continue its
work and ensure that the State is adequately prepared to address ongoing and anticipated wildland
fire emergencies.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New
Mexico and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution, by
the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE an emergency situation exists and ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred fifty thousand dollars ($750,000.00)
to the to the Forestry Division of the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department in
accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25. Funds shall be expended for the purpose
of wildland fire disaster relief, post-fire rehabilitation, adequate preparation, including pre-
positioning to deal with such disasters as a project, or for securing matching funds for emergencies;
and shall be expended specifically to avoid and minimize economic or physical harm and to protect
the public health, safety, and welfare. Funds shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary
of Finance and Administration upon vouchers approved by the Governor or an agent or agency

designated by her for that purpose.
